title: project.yaml schema for Rheoscope
description: Validates project.yaml before substitution. See Decision V2-4 (capabilities toggle), V2-5 (handoffs and kickoff-orchestration not valid capability keys).

project_slug.description: Lowercase slug. Must start with a-z or 0-9; subsequent chars a-z, 0-9, hyphen.

capabilities.description: Opt-in capability toggles. Keys MUST be exactly the set declared. handoffs is not a capability (always core). kickoff-orchestration is not a capability (documentation-only).

personnel.description: At least one personnel entry. Each is identity + role + domain-ownership.

tag.description: Short identifier used as a raw-file source tag.

domains_owned.description: Wiki subdirectories this person is review authority for. Use ['*'] for all-domains.

wiki_domains.description: Wiki subdirectory definitions (only meaningful when capabilities.knowledge-os is true).

corpus_source.description: Execution-corpus identifier (org/repo), or 'none'. Only meaningful with knowledge-os enabled, when the project's execution plane lives in a separate sibling repo whose shipped-state the wiki observes. Read at runtime by /flight-plan, /compile, /audit; NOT init-substituted. See docs/wiki-schema.md § 16.

corpus_config.description: Required when corpus_source is not 'none'. Legacy singular form — projects with more than one execution repo use corpus_sources instead.

corpus_sources.description: Multi-corpus binding (v3.0.18, backlog v3.0-88): one entry per execution-plane repo the wiki observes. Each corpus keeps its own identity and its own last-reconciled SHA row in wiki/HEALTH.md § Corpus Observation; every consumer (/flight-plan, /compile, /audit, /doctor) reports each corpus independently and surfaces an unreachable declared corpus VISIBLY — partial observation is never silent. Mutually exclusive with a non-'none' corpus_source (declaring both is a config error). The singular corpus_source + corpus_config form stays valid for one-repo projects.

id.description: Stable short identifier for HEALTH rows and briefings. Defaults to the repo name segment of source.

source.description: org/repo identifier of this execution corpus.

clone_path.description: Local clone used for read-only observation.

template_version.description: Harness template version (provenance) — a quoted string matching the template's root VERSION file at instantiation time. Permissive by design — the schema is NOT the version gate and deliberately carries no version literal of its own. init.ps1/init.sh compare this field against VERSION (the single version source, consumed at init) and emit a migration-aware message on mismatch; project.yaml.example ships the current value. Kept loose here so the schema validates a project.yaml authored against any harness version.

template_source.description: Public template repository URL (v3.0.12, backlog v3.0-59). Stamped by init; the address 'check for updates' resolves against. Empty string on pre-v3.0.12 instances until backfilled.

template_release.description: The template release tag this instance actually runs (e.g. v3.0.12). Stamped by init from the template tree's RELEASE file; advanced by adoption sessions in the same commit as each file-level adoption. Distinct from template_version, which tracks the major/minor contract and does not move on patch adoption.

instantiated_date.description: Stamped by init at instantiation time (ISO 8601). Empty pre-instantiation.

placeholder_scan_exempt.description: Relative paths or path-prefixes (from repo root) that init-validate skips when scanning for unresolved {{...}} placeholders. For META docs that legitimately contain literal placeholder syntax (the init scripts, build logs, this example file). A trailing '/' denotes a directory prefix. Operators append project-specific files that document the convention.

dependency_scan_skip.description: Directory NAMES that init-validate's {{...}} placeholder scan skips wherever they appear at any depth (case-sensitive segment match, not prefix). For vendored/generated dirs (node_modules, .next, build, dist, ...) whose third-party content would otherwise yield false unresolved-placeholder failures. The single source both validators (powershell-yaml + yq) read, so both consume the identical set; the match is case-sensitive on both sides and a scalar (non-list) value is ignored by both. .git is always skipped separately. See v3.0-14.

trust_surface_signing.description: The project's AUTHORITY MODE -- an explicit one-time operator choice (v3.0.49; ADR #11 condition 4 as amended 2026-08-22, backlog v3.0-135). There is NO silent default: init asks once and writes the answer (or --authority-mode=visible|required / -AuthorityMode); when ABSENT, HUMAN-GATE consumers run in migration-only `warn` (accept + surface a WARNING line) and content RETIREMENT IS DISABLED (deploy/trust.py refuses publication) until you record a choice -- /doctor check 16 and /sweep step 17 keep naming it. `visible`: reversible-and-visible -- no signature expected, nothing warned; every sensor (committed-identity, append-only journal, first-parent retirement reader, rewind detector, doctor 16, sweep 17) still runs, and a retirement waits for one exact-digest promote action from you per batch (Release 2). `required`: the hardware-key root -- every trust-surface commit and retirement tag must verify against core/security/hooks/allowed_signers with a presence-requiring (sk) key (run the MIGRATION v3.0.45 -> v3.0.46 ceremony first). `warn`: migration-only compatibility for instances born before v3.0.49; not a settled choice for a new project. Committed-identical (working tree == HEAD) is required under every mode.

observation_window_days.description: Optional (v3.0.50; ADR #11 condition 4 as amended 2026-08-22, backlog v3.0-139). The OBSERVATION WINDOW in days for the durable pending list (deploy/pending.py): every retirement and trust-surface change on the production branch is reconstructed from git objects and stays pending until an ATTENDED sweep renders it (reading the sweep is the acknowledgement; an unattended/scheduled sweep renders but never acknowledges). When no attended sweep has closed ok within this many days, the independent observer (the nightly standing-loop tick, `pending.py --observe`) writes a missed-cycle alarm row that is itself pending until acknowledged; a failed sweep cycle raises a failed-cycle alarm regardless of the window. Default 7 when absent. /doctor check 16 (alarm sub-check) and /sweep step 17 name a missed window.

production_branch.description: Optional (v3.0.52, backlog v3.0-151, fleet inbox #8). The PRODUCTION BRANCH the retirement machinery publishes to and reads from (deploy/retire.py, promote.py, pending.py, doctor 16(f), every echoed command). When absent, the machinery resolves the CHECKED-OUT branch (symbolic-ref HEAD) -- correct for almost every instance, including non-main branches like a dogfood fork. Set this only when the checkout routinely sits on a branch other than the production one. An explicit --branch flag always wins; an unresolvable branch REFUSES (never a silent `main`).

backlog_upstream.description: Optional. GitHub owner/repo whose Issues serve as the fleet backlog inbox (v3.0-128). When set, /log-backlog files each new entry upstream via `gh issue create` in addition to the local append; when absent, /log-backlog is local-only (the pre-v3.0.44 behavior). Point this at a PRIVATE repo -- backlog entries may carry venture content.
